message.content: {"action":"done","summary":"Implemented tinydb/journal.py: BatchWriter(db) with apply(operations) targeting the default table only. R01: validates each op as {'op':'insert','document':Mapping} or {'op':'remove','doc_id':positive int (bool rejected)}; non-list batches, non-mapping entries, unknown/missing op, non-mapping document, and non-positive/non-int doc_id all raise ValueError; returns inserted IDs in order, removes add nothing, empty batch returns []. R02: atomic — deep-copies pre-batch storage state, applies sequentially, on any error (incl. remove of missing ID, checked explicitly since Table.remove skips missing IDs) restores full state via storage.write(snapshot) and resets table._next_id so previously acquired db.table('_default') handles see both success and rollback (handles read from storage per op). R03: ordinary TinyDB APIs untouched (new module only, no upstream edits); inserted docs stored via deepcopy so caller input is not aliased; after-apply mutation of ops cannot mutate the database. Tests: tests/test_journal.py (38 tests) covering all three user stories, rollback edge cases, pre-acquired handle visibility, other-table preservation, and data independence. Evidence: `python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -o addopts= -q` → 263 passed (includes 2 acceptance_public tests and all upstream tests). Unresolved: tasks.md checkbox updates were not performed this phase (the file's task list lives in the workflow artifacts and the phase budget ended before editing it); checklist gate passed (checklists/requirements.md all [x]); no .specify/extensions.yml hooks exist to run. One test nuance documented in-test: returned Document instances share nested objects with live storage, so the aliasing test only asserts caller-input independence, per spec R03."}
